headline: A paper models GPU energy per output token from active bytes and decode time
summary: A new arXiv paper proposes a locally calibrated model for GPU-board energy per useful output token during dense, full-history decoding. It combines shared-weight bytes, per-request KV-history bytes and observed decode time. The authors report 374 held-out energy executions in total: 270 static workload runs across 54 conditions (maximum condition-mean error 3.73%) and 104 controlled request-departure runs (all condition-mean errors below 1%). A separate 177 HBM profiles examine whether the logical byte coordinates track physical reads. Results cover three BF16 models and specified GH200/GB300 configurations; they do not establish independent reproduction, portable coefficients, facility energy or monetary savings.
